expansionNote: Replaces the 5 hand-seeded placeholder questions with a 35-question bank authored using the construction-specific material from the NCERT Exemplar Unit 5 'Understanding Quadrilaterals and Practical Geometry' (practical.pdf), deliberately excluding general quadrilateral-property material already covered by Understanding Quadrilaterals' own 40-question bank. No canonical-topic.json exists for this chapter (topicId is null throughout) - see stage2-topic-detection.md for the architectural reason and how this bank is merged into runtime data outside the normal Stage 10 pipeline. Difficulty split: 12 Easy (34%), 15 Medium (43%), 8 Hard (23%). All answers are single short values (a number, a short phrase, or Yes/No/True/False) to stay reliably compatible with the exact-string-match evaluator.

questions.prompt: Which instrument is used to draw arcs and circles?
hints: This instrument has two pointed legs and a pencil arm.
It's the same tool used to mark off a fixed radius.

questions.prompt: Which instrument is used to draw a line segment of a given length?
hints: This tool has markings in centimetres for measuring straight-line distances.

questions.prompt: Which instrument is used to measure or construct an angle of a given size?
hints: This tool has a semicircular scale marked in degrees.
It's placed with its centre at the vertex of the angle.

questions.prompt: What do you call a ray that divides an angle into two equal parts?
hints: It creates two equal smaller angles from one larger angle.

questions.prompt: What two pieces of information must you know to draw a unique circle?
hints: Think about what you set the compass to, and where you place its point.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum number of measurements needed to construct a quadrilateral uniquely?
hints: A quadrilateral has 4 sides and 2 diagonals — but not all of these are independent measurements.
This is the general rule stated for quadrilaterals with no special properties.

questions.prompt: Can a quadrilateral be constructed uniquely if only the lengths of its 4 sides are known (no angle or diagonal)?
hints: A quadrilateral's shape can flex even if all four side lengths stay fixed — think of a hinge.
You need a fifth measurement (a diagonal or an angle) to fix the shape.

questions.prompt: Can a quadrilateral be constructed uniquely given its four sides and one diagonal?
hints: This is one of the four standard measurement combinations for constructing a quadrilateral.

questions.prompt: Can a quadrilateral be constructed uniquely given three sides and two diagonals?
hints: This is one of the four standard measurement combinations for constructing a quadrilateral.

questions.prompt: Can a quadrilateral be constructed uniquely given two adjacent sides and three angles?
hints: This is one of the four standard measurement combinations for constructing a quadrilateral.

questions.prompt: Can a quadrilateral be constructed uniquely given three sides and the two angles included between them?
hints: This is one of the four standard measurement combinations for constructing a quadrilateral.

questions.prompt: How many triangles is a quadrilateral split into when one diagonal is drawn?
hints: A diagonal connects two opposite vertices, cutting the quadrilateral in two.

questions.prompt: In the 4-sides-and-1-diagonal construction method, each of the two triangles is drawn using which triangle congruence rule: SSS, SAS, or ASA?
hints: Each triangle is built from three known side lengths — two sides of the quadrilateral plus the shared diagonal.
No angle is given directly in this method, only side lengths.

questions.prompt: A quadrilateral ABCD is being constructed with diagonal BD splitting it into triangle ABD and triangle BCD. If angle ABD = 40 degrees and angle DBC = 35 degrees, what is the full angle ABC?
hints: Angle ABC is made up of the two smaller angles on either side of the diagonal BD.
Add the two given angles together.

questions.prompt: A parallelogram PQRS is being constructed with PQ = 5 cm, QR = 4 cm and angle PQR = 70 degrees. What is the measure of the adjacent angle QRS?
hints: Adjacent angles in a parallelogram are supplementary — they add up to 180 degrees.
Subtract the given angle from 180 degrees.

questions.prompt: A rectangle is to be constructed with one side 6 cm and a diagonal of 10 cm. What is the length of the other side?
hints: A rectangle's diagonal, together with two adjacent sides, forms a right triangle.
Use the Pythagorean relation: diagonal² = side² + side².

questions.prompt: A rhombus is to be constructed with diagonals of 6 cm and 8 cm. What is the length of each side?
hints: A rhombus's diagonals bisect each other at right angles, forming four right triangles.
Use half of each diagonal as the two legs of a right triangle, and the Pythagorean relation to find the side.

questions.prompt: A rhombus is being constructed with side 5 cm, using a diagonal of 6 cm to split it into two triangles. Is each of those triangles equilateral, isosceles, or scalene?
hints: Each triangle has two sides that are sides of the rhombus (so they're equal to each other) and a base that's the diagonal.
A triangle with exactly two equal sides is isosceles.

questions.prompt: True or False: a quadrilateral can be constructed uniquely knowing only its three sides and one diagonal (no angles given).
hints: Compare this to the four valid measurement combinations for constructing a quadrilateral.
3 sides and 1 diagonal is not enough — the valid combination needs 2 diagonals, not 1.

questions.prompt: True or False: a trapezium can sometimes be constructed by first drawing a triangle formed from the difference of its two parallel sides.
hints: This is a standard technique for trapezium construction when the two parallel sides and the legs are known.

questions.prompt: A trapezium is to be constructed with parallel sides of 9 cm and 5 cm. Using the difference-of-parallel-sides technique, what length is used to start the construction triangle?
hints: Subtract the shorter parallel side from the longer one.

questions.prompt: Can a unique quadrilateral be constructed if only its four angles are given (no side lengths)?
hints: Angles alone fix the quadrilateral's shape but not its size.
Without at least one length measurement, the quadrilateral could be scaled to any size.

questions.prompt: Can a unique rectangle be constructed if only one side length is given?
hints: A rectangle's angles are already fixed at 90 degrees, but one side length alone doesn't fix the other side.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum number of measurements needed to construct a unique rectangle?
hints: A rectangle's angles are already fixed at 90 degrees, so you don't need to measure any angle.
You just need its length and its breadth.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum number of measurements needed to construct a unique parallelogram?
hints: Two adjacent sides and the angle between them are enough to fix a parallelogram completely.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum number of measurements needed to construct a unique square?
hints: A square's angles are all fixed at 90 degrees, and all its sides are equal by definition.
Only one length is needed.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum number of measurements needed to construct a unique rhombus?
hints: A rhombus's four sides are already equal by definition.
Either a side and one angle, or the two diagonals, are enough.

questions.prompt: In the '2 adjacent sides and 3 angles' construction method, how many of the quadrilateral's four vertex angles are directly given as measurements?
hints: The method's name tells you exactly how many angles are given.
The fourth angle is worked out afterward, not given directly.

questions.prompt: A quadrilateral is being constructed by the '2 adjacent sides and 3 angles' method. Three of its angles are given as 80, 95 and 100 degrees. What is the fourth angle?
hints: The interior angles of any quadrilateral add up to 360 degrees.
Add the three given angles, then subtract from 360.

questions.prompt: When constructing a square using its diagonals, the two equal diagonals are drawn bisecting each other at what angle?
hints: This is the same diagonal property that a rhombus has (a square is a special rhombus).

questions.prompt: A rectangle is to be constructed with sides 8 cm and 6 cm. What is the length of each diagonal?
hints: A rectangle's diagonal, together with two adjacent sides, forms a right triangle.
Use the Pythagorean relation: diagonal² = side² + side².

questions.prompt: A rhombus is to be constructed with diagonals of 10 cm and 24 cm. What is the length of each side?
hints: A rhombus's diagonals bisect each other at right angles, forming four right triangles.
Use half of each diagonal as the two legs of a right triangle, and the Pythagorean relation to find the side.

questions.prompt: A rhombus is to be constructed with side 8 cm and one angle of 60 degrees. What is the measure of the adjacent angle?
hints: A rhombus is a parallelogram, so adjacent angles are supplementary.
Subtract the given angle from 180 degrees.

questions.prompt: True or False: every quadrilateral has exactly two diagonals.
hints: A diagonal connects two non-adjacent vertices.
A quadrilateral has 4 vertices — count how many non-adjacent pairs that gives.

questions.prompt: A parallelogram is constructed with adjacent sides 6 cm and 8 cm, and the included angle is 90 degrees. What special quadrilateral results?
hints: A parallelogram with one 90-degree angle automatically has all four angles at 90 degrees.
The two adjacent sides are different lengths (6 cm and 8 cm), so it isn't a square.
